title: Mara and the Veil
premise: Emrys Thackeray, a mercenary sworn to a silent god and trapped in the magicless valley of Vaelmoor, discovers his name in a century-old book of prophecies owned by Mara Quill, the last archivist of a country that was erased from maps and memory. Together they must find the Veil-door that leads out of the vanished nation before its dying magic consumes them both — but the prophecy demands one of them stay behind as the door's anchor. In the end, Emrys chooses to break his oath rather than sacrifice Mara, shattering the prophecy itself; the door opens not through obedience but through refusal, and they walk out into a world that has forgotten them, carrying the last true record of the country that no longer exists.
about_author: Petra Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned estate libraries in northern England before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about forgotten places, stubborn records, and the people who refuse to let either be erased.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A routine contract in the valley of Vaelmoor goes wrong when Emrys realizes his god's blessing — dormant for years — has fully failed him mid-fight. He spares a target he should have killed, breaking mercenary code. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional detachment; the first crack in a life built on an oath.

chapters.title: A Book That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In her hidden archive beneath the ruined capital of Cindralle — a country no map remembers — Mara finds a prophecy book written a century ago, naming 'the Thackeray man' and tonight's date. Terrified and exhilarated, she performs the summoning rite it describes. Emotional beat: obsessive hope; she has waited her whole life to matter to something.

chapters.title: Pulled Through
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Mid-journey, Emrys is wrenched out of Vaelmoor into Cindralle's twilight streets, where magic works again for the first time in his life. He meets Mara, who shows him his own name in the old book. He wants only to go home; she says the way home runs deeper in. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into anger at being used.

chapters.title: What the Erasure Took
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara guides Emrys toward the Veil-door while explaining the Erasure: Cindralle traded its existence to end a war, and everyone born after cannot remember it but her, bound by blood-oath as archivist. Emrys notices she flinches whenever he says her name aloud. Emotional beat: grief worn as duty; loneliness revealed.

chapters.title: The Company of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They shelter with the Hollowed — survivors of the Erasure who persist as half-remembered ghosts, including Sef, a child soldier who adopts Emrys with fierce, wordless loyalty. For the first time since his god went silent, Emrys feels needed rather than employed. Emotional beat: found family kindling against his will.

chapters.title: The Price Written Down
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Deciphering the prophecy's final page, Mara learns the Veil-door requires an anchor: one soul must remain inside Cindralle forever or the door seals and both die. The text names the anchor ambiguously — 'the keeper of the book.' She hides this from Emrys. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme turns inward; love as concealment.

chapters.title: Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The Warden of the Erasure — the entity that consumed Cindralle — offers Emrys a bargain: betray Mara, take the door alone, and return to Vaelmoor restored, his god's voice included. Emrys nearly accepts; the silence has hollowed him for years. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate; power offered as mercy.

chapters.title: Sef's Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Warden, denied Emrys, takes Sef instead, planning to use the child as the anchor. Mara breaks her archivist's oath and burns pages of the prophecy to buy time, discovering that burning the book weakens the Warden — and that the prophecy can be rewritten, not just fulfilled. Emotional beat: sacrilege as salvation; truth finally chosen over loyalty to the dead.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the Veil-door, Emrys learns everything — the anchor clause, Mara's concealment, Sef's capture. Instead of choosing between them, he publicly renounces his god and swears himself to no oath at all, declaring the prophecy void. The Warden, built on binding oaths, begins to unravel. Emotional beat: climax; freedom found in breaking, not keeping, faith.

chapters.title: Out of the Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the Warden dissolving, Mara rewrites the final line — 'no one remains' — and the door opens wide enough for all three. They step into Vaelmoor's dawn, carrying Cindralle's last book, unremembered by the world but known to each other. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; a found family as the only country left worth belonging to.
